mainTopic: Respect for a בית הכנסת, blessings in the מקדש, greeting with God's name, 'עת לעשות לה׳', practical life lessons, and the story of חנינא setting the calendar in בבל
overview: This amud moves through many short topics. First, the גמרא finishes a discussion about respect for a בית הכנסת. רבא concludes that it is like a person's own house: a shortcut through it is forbidden, but spitting and wearing shoes are allowed. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה about the מקדש. Blessings there had a long special ending because people did not answer אמן there; each blessing got its own full praise, based on a פסוק in נחמיה. The גמרא then explains why the משנה brings several פסוקים to allow greeting with God's name. It also explains the פסוק 'עת לעשות לה׳', which רבא reads in two directions and הלל uses to teach when to spread Torah and when to hold back. A series of life lessons follows from בר קפרא, רבי, רבי יוחנן and others: lead where no one else leads, keep ה׳ in mind in everything, give your gifts to the כהן, and turn to ה׳ in times of trouble. The amud ends with the story of חנינא, who set the calendar in בבל. The חכמים of ארץ ישראל send messengers who warn him to stop or be placed in נידוי.

steps.title: Challenge: Why not learn the stricter rule for a בית הכנסת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges learning the בית הכנסת rules from the הר הבית. It argues that a בית הכנסת should forbid spitting, because it can be compared to the shortcut rule instead of the shoe rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this: for the הר הבית, where shoes are forbidden, it makes sense to learn the spitting rule from shoes. But a בית הכנסת allows shoes. So instead of learning from shoes and being lenient, let us learn from the shortcut rule and be strict!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier comparison between the בית הכנסת and the הר הבית. If spitting on the הר הבית is learned from shoes, then a בית הכנסת should instead be compared to shortcuts, and spitting there should be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the הר הבית, spitting is forbidden by a קל וחומר from shoes: if mere shoes are forbidden, surely spitting is. In a בית הכנסת, shoes are allowed, but taking a shortcut (קפנדריא) is forbidden. The challenge asks why we would pick the lenient model (shoes) rather than the strict model (shortcut) to decide about spitting.

keyTerms.meaning: But say / why not say (introduces an alternative reading that challenges the previous one)
A shortcut (cutting through a place just to get somewhere faster)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is questioning the shoe rule itself. Everyone agrees that shoes are forbidden on the הר הבית and allowed in a בית הכנסת. The only question is which of these known rules spitting should be compared to.

phrases.english: But say: the Temple Mount, where it is forbidden to wear shoes —
phrases.notes: Opens the challenge

phrases.english: let it learn [the spitting rule] from shoes.
phrases.notes: For the הר הבית, the comparison to shoes works.

phrases.english: But a synagogue, where shoes are permitted,
instead of learning from shoes and being lenient,
let us learn from the shortcut and be strict!
phrases.notes: In a בית הכנסת, shortcuts are forbidden, so spitting should be forbidden too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous derivation (earlier) that compared the בית הכנסת to the הר הבית.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attempt to learn the בית הכנסת rules for spitting and shoes from the הר הבית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison can go two ways. Since the בית הכנסת allows shoes but forbids shortcuts, it could just as easily be compared to the strict rule (shortcuts). Then spitting there would be forbidden, so the comparison does not lead to a clear lenient result.

steps.title: רבא: A בית הכנסת is like one's own house
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the comparison to the הר הבית. Instead, he compares a בית הכנסת to a person's house: shortcuts are forbidden, but spitting and shoes are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: a בית הכנסת is like a person's house. A person minds when others use his house as a shortcut, but he does not mind spitting or shoes there. So too in a בית הכנסת: a shortcut is forbidden, but spitting and shoes are allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the comparison to the הר הבית ran into trouble, רבא gives a completely new source for the rules of a בית הכנסת. He uses a person's house as the model.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier approach is set aside. A house is a good model because it explains both rules at once: what an ordinary homeowner minds (a shortcut) is forbidden, and what he does not mind (spitting, shoes) is allowed. This solves the problem from step 1, because we no longer have to choose between two competing comparisons.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals dropping the previous approach for a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: The final model for a בית הכנסת is a person's own house. Using it as a shortcut is forbidden. Spitting and wearing shoes there are permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the standard used for practical halacha: respect for a בית הכנסת is measured by what a person would mind in his own home.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: [a synagogue is] like his house —
just as with his house, a person objects to a shortcut,
but about spitting and shoes a person does not object,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת, קַפֶּנְדַּרְיָא הוּא דַּאֲסִיר,
phrases.english: so too a synagogue: it is a shortcut that is forbidden,
while spitting and shoes are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by replacing the הר הבית comparison with a new one: a person's own house.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the source of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בית הכנסת rules were learned from the הר הבית. That created a choice between the shoe model and the shortcut model.
steps.terutzMaskana: The בית הכנסת is modeled on a private home. Shortcuts are forbidden; spitting and shoes are permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a בית הכנסת, a shortcut is forbidden, but spitting and shoes are permitted.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about blessings in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about how blessings were ended in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] At the end of all blessings said in the מקדש, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the opening words of the משנה. This is a setup line: the next steps will explain this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that blessings in the מקדש had a special, longer ending. It said they would end with "עד העולם", and later this was changed to "מן העולם ועד העולם". The "וכו׳" tells us the rest of the משנה is assumed. The גמרא now wants to explain why such a special ending was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the rest of the quoted text is assumed)

phrases.english: All the conclusions of blessings in the Temple, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotation of the משנה that the גמרא will now explain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the בית הכנסת discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blessings in the מקדש were closed with a special formula about "the world" (עד העולם / מן העולם ועד העולם).

steps.title: Why was such a long ending needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the blessings in the מקדש needed such an extended ending.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why all this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the משנה: why did the מקדש need this long special closing? This line prepares the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary blessings end simply. The גמרא wants to know what was different about the מקדש. This is a real request for a reason, not an attack on the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Why so much? / Why to this extent?

phrases.english: Why all this —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מקדש blessings had a long, special ending.

steps.title: Because no one answers אמן in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in the מקדש people did not answer אמן, so the blessings needed a different, fuller ending.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because in the מקדש people do not answer אמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The special ending exists because in the מקדש, people did not respond with a simple אמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, people responded to a blessing with a long praise instead of אמן. Because the response was grander, the closing of the blessing was made grander too.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean people stayed silent in the מקדש. They gave a longer response of praise instead of אמן.

phrases.english: Because one does not answer "Amen" in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The special ending was needed because אמן is not the response in the מקדש.

steps.title: What is the source that אמן is not said in the מקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a scriptural source for the rule that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that people do not answer אמן in the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: Having stated the rule, the גמרא now asks where it comes from. This sets up the פסוק brought in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ומנין is the standard way to ask for a source in the Torah or Tanach. The rule itself is accepted; only its source is being requested.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know? (request for a source)

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one does not answer Amen in the Temple? —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule given in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אמן is not the response in the מקדש.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק in נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in נחמיה about blessing God "from everlasting to everlasting". The same פסוק continues that His name is exalted above all blessing and praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Stand up and bless ה׳ your God from everlasting to everlasting." And it says: "And let them bless Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rule with a פסוק in נחמיה. The פסוק describes a blessing that ends "from everlasting to everlasting" and a response that is greater than ordinary praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the פסוק matches the special closing used in the מקדש: "מן העולם עד העולם". The second part, "exalted above all blessing and praise", shows that the response to such a blessing must be a full praise. A simple אמן is not enough, and each blessing gets its own praise.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
And it says (continues with more of the פסוק)
Exalted above every blessing and praise

steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש, blessings ended with "מן העולם ועד העולם". People answered with a full praise instead of אמן. The source is the פסוק in נחמיה (9:5).

phrases.english: As it is said: "Stand up and bless the Lord your God
from everlasting to everlasting."
phrases.notes: נחמיה 9:5. This matches the closing formula used in the מקדש.

phrases.english: And it says: "And let them bless Your glorious name,
which is exalted above all blessing and praise."
phrases.notes: The response is greater than a simple אמן.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״קוּמוּ בָּרְכוּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם מִן הָעוֹלָם עַד הָעוֹלָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that אמן is not answered in the מקדש, and that blessings there have a special long ending.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה 9:5 — "קומו ברכו את ה׳ אלהיכם מן העולם עד העולם ויברכו שם כבודך ומרומם על כל ברכה ותהלה"

steps.title: Every blessing gets its own praise
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the פסוק in נחמיה teaches that each blessing in the מקדש needs its own separate praise, not one shared response.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that all the blessings together get one single praise. So the פסוק says: 'exalted above all blessing and praise.' This means: for every single blessing, give Him a praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes reading the פסוק from נחמיה that it began in the last step. It shows what the second half of the פסוק adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this phrase, we might think one short response, like אמן, could cover all the blessings. The words 'above all blessing and praise' teach that each blessing gets its own praise. That is why in the מקדש the blessing itself closed with the long formula 'מן העולם ועד העולם', and the people answered with a full praise ('ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד', see תענית טז:) instead of אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought'. It introduces a wrong first assumption.
'The verse teaches'. It introduces the scriptural correction.

steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש people did not answer אמן. Each blessing received its own full praise, because the פסוק says 'above all blessing and praise.'

phrases.english: I might have thought that all the blessings together
would have one single praise
Therefore the verse teaches:
"And exalted above all blessing and praise"
phrases.notes: נחמיה 9:5

phrases.english: meaning: for each and every blessing
give Him a praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל כׇּל הַבְּרָכוֹת כּוּלָּן תְּהֵא לָהֶן תְּהִלָּה אַחַת, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the פסוק in נחמיה that was begun in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Each blessing in the מקדש requires its own full praise, so אמן is not the response there.

steps.title: The משנה: greeting a friend with God's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the חכמים instituted that a person greets a friend using God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים instituted that a person should greet his friend (using God's name), and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, about greeting people with God's name. This quote sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that one may say God's name in a greeting, such as 'ה׳ עִמָּכֶם'. It supports this with a chain of פסוקים, each one introduced with 'וְאוֹמֵר'. The 'וְכוּ׳' tells us the גמרא is pointing to that whole passage.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They instituted'. It describes a rabbinic enactment.
Greets, literally 'asks after the welfare of'
'Etc.' The quote continues in the משנה.

phrases.english: They instituted that a person should
greet his friend (with God's name), etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם שׁוֹאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹם חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic from the משנה after finishing the topic of blessings in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may greet a friend using God's name.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need so many פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה keeps adding more פסוקים with 'וְאוֹמֵר' when it already brought the פסוק about בעז.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'? Why add more verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה brings extra פסוקים. The first proof, from בעז, already seemed to be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first proves its point from בעז, who greeted his harvesters with 'ה׳ עִמָּכֶם'. If that is a good proof, why does the משנה need 'וְאוֹמֵר' again and again? The question is about the structure of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says'. It introduces an additional פסוק.

phrases.english: What is the purpose of "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording and structure of the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה needs several proof-verses instead of just the בעז verse.

steps.title: בעז might have acted on his own, so the פסוק about גדעון is added
steps.stepSummary: The בעז proof could be dismissed as his personal choice, so the משנה adds the פסוק said to גדעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that בעז said this on his own (and his practice is not a proof), come and hear: "ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. Each extra פסוק closes a weakness in the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone could argue that בעז simply decided by himself to use God's name, so we cannot learn a rule from him. So the משנה adds the פסוק where גדעון is greeted with 'ה׳ עִמְּךָ', which shows the greeting coming from outside בעז's own choice.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say'. It raises a possible objection.
'Come and hear'. It introduces a proof.

phrases.english: And if you say that בעז
said this on his own initiative,
come and hear:
"ה׳ is with you, mighty man of valor."
phrases.notes: שופטים 6:12

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא בֹּעַז מִדַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ קָאָמַר, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק covers the weakness that בעז may have acted on his own.

steps.title: The angel's words may not be a greeting, so 'Do not despise your mother' is added
steps.stepSummary: The גדעון proof could be dismissed because an angel was only telling him a fact. So the משנה adds a פסוק teaching that we follow the practices of our elders, such as בעז.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it was an angel who said this to גדעון (as information, not as a greeting), come and hear: "Do not despise your mother when she is old."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the chain. It shows why the third פסוק is needed after the גדעון proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the angel was simply informing גדעון that God was with him, so it was not a normal greeting at all. The פסוק 'do not despise your mother when she is old' teaches that the customs of our nation's elders are a valid source. That brings back the בעז proof: his practice is one we may learn from.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'do not despise your mother' is not about greetings at all. It is used to show that we may rely on the practices of earlier generations, like בעז.

phrases.english: And if you say it was an angel
who said this to גדעון,
come and hear:
"Do not despise (her) because your mother is old."
phrases.notes: משלי 23:22

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַלְאָךְ הוּא דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ לְגִדְעוֹן, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer by closing the gap left in the גדעון proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third פסוק shows that the practice of the elders is authoritative, which supports the greeting custom.
steps.whatToRemember: Each 'וְאוֹמֵר' in the משנה closes a gap: בעז might have acted alone, so גדעון is added; the angel might only have been informing, so 'respect your elders' is added.

steps.title: The משנה's final פסוק: 'A time to act for ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's last proof-פסוק: 'It is time to act for ה׳; they have voided Your Torah.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And it says: "It is time to act for ה׳; they have voided Your Torah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last פסוק that the משנה brought. This sets up רבא's comment, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק teaches that sometimes, to serve God, we may do something that looks like going against the usual rules. Using God's name in a casual greeting is one such case. The גמרא now focuses on how to read this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A time to act for ה׳

phrases.english: And it says: "It is time to act for ה׳;
they have voided Your Torah."
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:126

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the final verse in the משנה's chain of proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is a time to act for ה׳, normal limits may be set aside.

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק reads both forward and backward
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that this פסוק can be explained from beginning to end, and also from end to beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This verse can be explained from its beginning to its end, and from its end to its beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a statement about how to read the פסוק. Each direction gives a different lesson, and the גמרא will explain both next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read from start to end, the reason is the second half: it is time to act for ה׳ because people have voided the Torah. Read from end to start, the reason is the first half: one may 'void' the Torah because it is a time to act for ה׳. רבא only states that both readings work here; the next two steps spell them out.

keyTerms.meaning: From its beginning to its end
From its end to its beginning

phrases.english: רבא said:
This verse
can be interpreted from its beginning to its end,
and can be interpreted from its end to its beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי קְרָא, מֵרֵישֵׁיהּ לְסֵיפֵיהּ מִדְּרִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the verse quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse 'עֵת לַעֲשׂוֹת לַה׳ הֵפֵרוּ תּוֹרָתֶךָ' can be expounded in either direction.

steps.title: Reading the verse from beginning to end
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the פסוק is explained by the second half: we act for ה׳ because people have voided the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read from beginning to end: 'It is time to act for ה׳.' Why? Because 'they have voided Your Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first of the two readings that רבא mentioned. Here, the beginning of the פסוק is the action and the end is the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because people have abandoned the Torah, it is time to act for ה׳ and fix the situation. In this reading, the breakdown in Torah observance is what pushes us to act.

keyTerms.meaning: From its beginning to its end

phrases.english: It can be explained from its beginning to its end:
'It is time to act for the Lord.' What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The first half of the verse is treated as the action.

phrases.english: Because 'they have voided Your Torah.'
phrases.notes: The second half is treated as the reason.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first of the two readings רבא mentioned in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the Torah is being abandoned, it is time to act for ה׳.

steps.title: Reading the verse from end to beginning
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the פסוק is explained by the first half: people may set aside a Torah rule because it is a time to act for ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read from end to beginning: 'They have voided Your Torah.' Why? Because 'it is time to act for ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second reading. Now the voiding of the Torah is the action, and acting for ה׳ is the reason that allows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the פסוק permits something surprising. Sometimes a Torah rule may be set aside, because doing so serves ה׳ at that moment. This is exactly how the משנה used the פסוק: to justify an unusual practice, such as greeting others with the name of ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: From its end to its beginning

steps.confusionAlert: This reading does NOT mean people randomly break Torah rules. It means that in special moments, setting aside a rule can itself be a way of serving ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק gives two lessons. (1) Because the Torah is being abandoned, we must act for ה׳. (2) Because it is a time to act for ה׳, a Torah rule may sometimes be set aside.

phrases.english: It can be explained from its end to its beginning:
'They have voided Your Torah.' What is the reason?
Because 'it is time to act for the Lord.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse reading, completing רבא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because it is a time to act for ה׳, people may set aside a Torah rule.

steps.title: הלל: when to spread Torah and when to hold back
steps.stepSummary: הלל הזקן teaches that one should spread Torah when others hold back, and hold back when others spread it. One should spread Torah to a generation that loves it, and hold back from a generation that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that הלל הזקן said: When others gather in (hold back), you spread out. When others spread out, you gather in. If you see a generation that loves Torah, spread it, as the פסוק says, 'There is one who scatters and gains more.' If you see a generation that does not love Torah, hold back, as it says, 'It is time to act for ה׳; they have voided Your Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same פסוק, 'עת לעשות לה׳', for a new lesson. It is about when to teach Torah publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל gives two guidelines. First, balance what others are doing: teach if no one else is teaching, and step back if others already are. Second, judge the audience: teach a generation that cherishes Torah, but hold back from one that would treat it with disrespect. Holding back in that case is itself 'acting for ה׳'.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the פסוק used in practice. Sometimes holding back Torah, which seems like a loss, is actually done for the sake of ה׳.

phrases.english: It was taught: Hillel the Elder says:
At a time when others gather in, scatter.
phrases.notes: When the sages are holding Torah back, you should spread it.

phrases.english: At a time when others scatter, gather in.
phrases.notes: When others are already teaching, you may step back.

phrases.english: And if you see a generation
for whom the Torah is beloved, scatter,
as it says: 'There is one who scatters, and yet gains more' (משלי 11:24).
And if you see a generation
for whom the Torah is not beloved, gather in,
as it says: 'It is time to act for the Lord; they have voided Your Torah.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching built on the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spread Torah when it is cherished or when others hold back. Hold back when it is not cherished or when others are already spreading it.

steps.title: בר קפרא: buy when cheap, lead where no one leads
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches two practical sayings: when prices drop, jump and buy; and where there is no leader, be the leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: When it gets cheap, jump and buy from it. In a place where there is no man, there be a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching from בר קפרא. Like הלל, he says to take action when something is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sayings share one idea: grab the opportunity that others are leaving. If no one is filling a needed role, take responsibility yourself.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where there is no man (no leader)

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
When it becomes cheap, jump and buy from it;
in a place where there is no man,
there, be a man.
phrases.notes: Step up and fill the empty role.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a similar idea to הלל's first rule: act where others are not acting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where no one is leading, you should lead.

steps.title: אביי: where there is a leader, do not compete
steps.stepSummary: אביי infers the reverse of בר קפרא's saying: where someone already leads, you should not try to be the leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that in a place where there is a man, there do not be a man.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a reverse inference from בר קפרא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בר קפרא only said to lead 'where there is no man', then the reverse also follows. Where someone is already leading, step aside and do not compete with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is a man (a leader)

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that in a place where there is a man,
there, do not be a man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reverse inference from בר קפרא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not compete for leadership where a leader already exists.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: why would anyone need to be told this?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's statement as too obvious to be worth saying. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a capable leader is already in place, it seems clear that you should not push in. So what new lesson did אביי add?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's inference as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stepping aside where a leader already exists seems self-evident, so it should not need to be stated.

steps.title: Even when both are equally qualified
steps.stepSummary: אביי's point is needed for the case where you and the existing leader are equally qualified. Even then, do not compete.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for a case where both of them are equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining which case אביי was really teaching about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the existing leader is better than you, stepping aside is obvious. The new lesson is that even when you are just as qualified, you should not push in, since someone is already filling the role.

keyTerms.meaning: The two of them are equal

steps.whatToRemember: Take responsibility when no one else is doing so. But if someone is already filling the role, do not compete with him, even if you are just as qualified.

phrases.english: It was needed only
for a case where the two of them are equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that if you are equally qualified, you may compete for the role.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when both are equal, do not compete with someone who already holds the role.

steps.title: A short passage that all of Torah depends on
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא teaches that the whole תורה hangs on one short verse: 'In all your ways know Him, and He will straighten your paths.'
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: Which is a short passage that all the main parts of the תורה depend on? 'In all your ways know Him, and He will make your paths straight.'
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא asks which tiny passage holds up the whole תורה, and answers with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a person must keep הקב״ה in mind in everything he does, not only during davening or learning. If he does this, הקב״ה will guide his life. Because this attitude covers every action, it is the root of all the מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: The main bodies or fundamentals of the תורה
Hang on it, depend on it
Know Him, be aware of Him

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the idea that all of a person's daily activity can be done for the sake of Heaven.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
Which is a short passage
that all the fundamentals of Torah depend on it?
'In all your ways know Him,
and He will make your paths straight.'
phrases.notes: משלי ג:ו

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ בַּר קַפָּרָא: אֵיזוֹהִי פָּרָשָׁה קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of בר קפרא, added to the series of practical sayings that began earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse 'In all your ways know Him' is the short passage on which all of the תורה depends.

steps.title: Even for a matter of sin
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that 'In all your ways know Him' applies even to a דבר עבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even for a matter of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא stretches בר קפרא's verse to apply even to a situation involving an עבירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'all' in 'all your ways' includes even a case of sin. רש״י explains this as an act that looks like an עבירה but is done for the sake of Heaven, like אליהו bringing a קרבן outside the מקדש on הר הכרמל. Another explanation is that even while a person falls into sin, he should still keep הקב״ה in mind and not go further.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of sin or transgression

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is NOT permitting sin. He is saying that awareness of הקב״ה must be present even in that kind of situation.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even for a matter of transgression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the scope of the verse quoted by בר קפרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'In all your ways' includes even a matter of sin.

steps.title: Teach your son a clean and easy trade
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא advises that a person should always teach his son a trade that is clean and easy.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: A person should always teach his son a trade that is clean and easy.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא gives practical advice about choosing a job for one's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clean trade keeps a person away from dishonesty and from dirty, degrading work. An easy trade leaves energy and time for תורה. This step sets up the question in the next step: which trade is that?

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
A person should always teach his son
a clean and easy craft.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ בַּר קַפָּרָא: לְעוֹלָם יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching of בר קפרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father should teach his son a clean and easy trade.

steps.title: Which trade is that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which specific trade counts as clean and easy.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא gave a general description but no example. The גמרא wants a concrete trade so the advice can actually be followed.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a concrete example of בר קפרא's 'clean and easy trade.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific trade is considered clean and easy.

steps.title: רב חסדא names the trade
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the trade is מחטא דתלמיותא, a fine needle craft.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The needle of furrows, meaning fine needlework.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the example the גמרא asked for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רש״י explains this as fine needlework that makes delicate lines. The Sefaria translation renders it as cutting precious stones. Either way, it is light, neat work that does not dirty a person or wear him out.
steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא: teach your son a clean, easy trade. רב חסדא: an example is fine needlework (or gem cutting).

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
The needle of furrows (fine needlework / gem cutting).
phrases.notes: רש״י: fine needlework; Sefaria: cutting precious stones

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clean and easy trade is fine needle craft.

steps.title: Do not bring too many friends into your house
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: a person should not have too many friends in his house, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: A person should never have too many friends in his house, as it says: 'A man with many friends will come to harm.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives advice about guests and friends in the home and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads the word להתרועע as 'to be broken' or 'to come to harm.' Too many close friends coming in and out of a house can lead to quarrels and damage, or can use up the host's resources.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
To come to harm, be broken

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
A person should never increase
friends within his house,
as it is stated: 'A man of many friends comes to harm.'
phrases.notes: משלי יח:כד

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אַל יַרְבֶּה אָדָם רֵעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new piece of practical advice, now from a ברייתא quoting רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not have too many friends in your house.

steps.title: Do not appoint a manager over your house
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches not to appoint an אפוטרופוס over one's household. He proves it from פוטיפר appointing יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי says: A person should not appoint a manager inside his house. If פוטיפר had not appointed יוסף as manager in his house, יוסף would not have come to that incident.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives another rule about running a home and backs it up with a story from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving an outsider full control inside the house brings him close to the family and can lead to trouble. The proof is פוטיפר: because יוסף ran his house, יוסף was there alone with פוטיפר's wife, which led to the accusation against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A manager or administrator of household affairs
To that incident (the episode with אשת פוטיפר)

steps.whatToRemember: This section is a chain of practical life advice: keep הקב״ה in mind in everything (even matters of sin), teach a clean trade, limit friends in your home, and do not hand your house over to a manager.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: אַל יְמַנֶּה אָדָם אַפֹּטְרוֹפּוֹס בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: A person should not appoint a manager within his house,
for had Potiphar not appointed
Joseph as manager within his house,
he would not have come to that incident.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אַל יְמַנֶּה אָדָם אַפֹּטְרוֹפּוֹס בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי about managing one's household, parallel to Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not appoint an אפוטרופוס inside your house, as shown by פוטיפר and יוסף.

steps.title: Why the section of נזיר comes right after the section of סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that the placement of פרשת נזיר right after פרשת סוטה tells us something. Whoever sees a סוטה in her disgrace should take a נזירות and stay away from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי says: Why was the section of the נזיר placed next to the section of the סוטה? To tell you that anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should make himself a נזיר and stay away from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי learns a life lesson from the fact that two sections of the Torah sit side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine can lead a person to lose control and sin, as happened with the סוטה. So the Torah puts the נזיר, who gives up wine, right after her story. Someone who has just seen where sin leads should build a fence for himself by giving up wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Was placed next to (the idea of סמיכות פרשיות)
A person who vows to stay away from wine, haircuts and טומאת מת
A wife suspected of being unfaithful

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Why was the section of the Nazirite placed next to
phrases.notes: פרשת נזיר is in במדבר chapter 6.

phrases.english: the section of the sota?
phrases.notes: פרשת סוטה is in במדבר chapter 5, just before.

phrases.english: To tell you
that anyone who sees a sota in her disgrace
should make himself a Nazirite, away from wine.
phrases.notes: Wine is one of the things that leads to this kind of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת נָזִיר לְפָרָשַׁת סוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of teachings from רבי (Steps 27-28) with another piece of practical advice for life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should take on נזירות and avoid wine.

steps.title: Holding back gifts from the כהן leads to needing the כהן through one's wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that פרשת סוטה sits next to the gifts for the כהן. Someone who keeps his תרומות ומעשרות will end up needing the כהן for his wife as a סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה, son of רבי פרנך, said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Why was the section of the סוטה placed next to the section of תרומות ומעשרות? To tell you that anyone who has תרומות ומעשרות and does not give them to the כהן will end up needing the כהן because of his wife. As the פסוק says: 'And every man's holy things shall be his,' and right after it: 'If any man's wife goes astray,' and it is written: 'Then the man shall bring his wife to the כהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second lesson from the order of the פרשיות. This time it is about why סוטה comes right after the gifts to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'his holy things shall be his' is read as describing a man who keeps his gifts for himself. Right after it comes the סוטה. In that process the husband must bring his wife to the כהן, so the man who avoided the כהן is now forced to come to him, measure for measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The portions of produce that must be given to the כהן and the לוי
In the end, he will eventually
His holy things (here, his gifts for the כהן)
And right next to it is

phrases.english: Ḥizkiya son of Rabbi Parnakh said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.english: Why was the section of the sota placed next to
the section of terumot and tithes?
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:9-10, right before the סוטה.

phrases.english: To tell you:
Anyone who has terumot and tithes
and does not give them to the priest,

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף נִצְרָךְ לַכֹּהֵן עַל יְדֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: will end up needing the priest because of his wife,
as it says: 'And every man's holy things shall be his,'
phrases.notes: Read as: he keeps them for himself.

phrases.aramaic: וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ ״אִישׁ אִישׁ כִּי תִשְׂטֶה אִשְׁתּוֹ״,
phrases.english: and next to it: 'If any man's wife goes astray,'
and it is written: 'Then the man shall bring his wife' (to the priest), etc.
phrases.notes: This is the proof that he now has to come to the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נִסְמְכָה פָּרָשַׁת סוֹטָה לְפָרָשַׁת תְּרוּמוֹת וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method of reading the order of the פרשיות, applied to the section just before סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who holds back תרומות ומעשרות from the כהן will end up needing the כהן through his wife becoming a סוטה.

steps.title: He will even end up needing those very gifts himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a further punishment. The stingy man will become poor and will need to receive these same gifts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, but in the end he will need them himself, as it says: 'And every man's holy things shall be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a second consequence to his teaching, using the very same פסוק in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time 'his holy things shall be his' is read as a punishment. The gifts will 'be his' because he will become poor and have to take them, such as מעשר עני. The man who would not give will end up as the one who receives.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also

steps.confusionAlert: The same פסוק (״וְאִישׁ אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו לוֹ יִהְיוּ״) is quoted twice. In Step 30 it describes the man keeping his gifts. Here it predicts that he will need those gifts as a poor man.

phrases.english: And not only that, but
in the end he will need them himself,
phrases.notes: He becomes poor and must take gifts meant for the needy.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And every man's holy things shall be his.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be seen as the end of Step 30's מימרא rather than a separate step.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא סוֹף שֶׁנִּצְרָךְ לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, harsher consequence to רבי יוחנן's teaching from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who withholds the gifts will end up poor and needing them himself.

steps.title: One who does give to the כהן will become rich
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the positive side. One who gives his gifts to the כהן will end up wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: And if he did give them, he will end up rich, as it says: 'Whatever a man gives to the כהן, it shall be his.' 'It shall be his' means much wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds the flip side of רבי יוחנן's teaching: the reward for someone who does give.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the same פסוק says 'whatever a man gives to the כהן, it shall be his.' רב נחמן reads 'shall be his' as a promise of great wealth. Giving does not make a person poorer; it brings him riches.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And if he gave them, he will end up becoming rich,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן לַכֹּהֵן לוֹ יִהְיֶה״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'Whatever a man gives to the priest, it shall be his,'
'it shall be his': much wealth.
phrases.notes: The extra words 'shall be his' are read as a promise of riches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to Steps 30-31: the reward for giving instead of the punishment for holding back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who gives his gifts to the כהן will become wealthy.

steps.title: Bringing ה׳ into one's distress doubles one's livelihood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר הקפר teaches that someone who turns to שם שמים in his time of trouble will have his livelihood doubled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר ברכיה said in the name of רבי אלעזר הקפר: Anyone who makes שם שמים a partner in his distress, they double his livelihood. As it says: 'And שדי will be with you in your troubles, and you will have doubled silver.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about prayer and trust in ה׳. A person who turns to ה׳ when he is in trouble will be repaid with a double livelihood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב is read as 'שדי בצריך': ה׳ is with you in your distress. Then 'כסף תועפות' is read as doubled silver, because the word תועפות sounds like the Aramaic איף, meaning 'double'. The person 'partners' with ה׳ by praying to Him in his trouble, and the reward is a doubled livelihood.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a partner of, includes
Read here as 'doubled' (like the Aramaic אִיף, double)

steps.whatToRemember: This section is a set of practical lessons. Sin starts small, so build fences such as avoiding wine. Giving to the כהן brings wealth, while holding back brings poverty and shame. Turning to ה׳ in hard times doubles one's livelihood.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Berekhya said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar:
Anyone who includes the Name of Heaven in his distress,
phrases.notes: This means he turns to ה׳ in prayer during hard times.

phrases.english: his livelihood is doubled for him.
As it says: 'And the Almighty will be in your troubles,'
phrases.notes: From איוב 22:25. בצריך is read as 'in your distress'.

phrases.english: and doubled silver will be yours.'
phrases.notes: תועפות is linked to איף, meaning double.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from rewards for giving gifts to a new topic: the reward for turning to ה׳ in times of trouble. It shares the theme of livelihood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who includes שם שמים in his distress will have his livelihood doubled.

steps.title: Livelihood flies to him like a bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains the same פסוק differently. The reward is that a person's פרנסה comes to him quickly, like a flying bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: His livelihood flies to him like a bird, as it says: "And silver תועפות to you."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a second reading of the word תועפות in the same פסוק. רבי אלעזר הקפר had read it as "doubled." He reads it as "flying."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that turning to שם שמים in trouble brings reward. They disagree only about what the word תועפות means. רבי שמואל בר נחמני connects it to the root עוף, "to fly," so the reward is that פרנסה arrives quickly and easily.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the פסוק, read here as "flying" (from עוף)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
his livelihood flies to him like a bird,
as it is said: "And silver toafot to you."
phrases.notes: The wordplay is תועפות / מעופפת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that רבי אלעזר הקפר used in step 33
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward for turning to שם שמים in trouble is that one's livelihood comes swiftly, like a bird in flight.

steps.title: One who slacks off in Torah has no strength on a day of trouble
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבי, quoting רבי יאשיה, teaches that whoever weakens himself from Torah will lack strength when trouble comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טבי said in the name of רבי יאשיה: Anyone who is lax in words of Torah will have no strength to stand on a day of trouble, as it says: "If you were lax, on the day of trouble your strength is narrow."
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. It is linked to the previous topic by the theme of a "day of trouble." Being lax in Torah leaves a person without strength in hard times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps showed the reward for turning to ה׳ in trouble. This step shows the opposite side. רבי יאשיה reads the פסוק in two parts: "you were lax" is the cause, and "your strength is narrow on the day of trouble" is the result.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes himself lax or weak
A day of trouble or distress

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya:
Anyone who is lax in matters of Torah,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בּוֹ כֹּחַ לַעֲמוֹד בְּיוֹם צָרָה,
phrases.english: will have no strength to stand on a day of trouble,
as it is said: "If you were lax, on the day of trouble your strength is small."
phrases.notes: משלי כ״ד:י׳

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טָבִי אָמַר רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New teaching linked by the shared theme of a "day of trouble"
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weakening oneself from Torah leads to lacking strength in times of distress.

steps.title: Even being lax in one מצוה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל extends the previous teaching. Even slacking off in a single מצוה brings this result, because the פסוק says "you were lax" without any limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי בר מתנה said in the name of שמואל: And even one מצוה, because it says "you were lax," which means in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל widens רבי יאשיה's teaching. It applies even to someone who is lax in just one מצוה, not only in Torah as a whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that the פסוק says only "הִתְרַפִּיתָ" and does not say what the person was lax in. So it covers any slackening at all, even a small one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי בַּר מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Ami bar Mattana said in the name of Shmuel:
And even a single מצוה,
as it is said "you were lax," in any case.
phrases.notes: The פסוק does not limit the laxness, so it applies to any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי בַּר מַתְנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל וַאֲפִילּוּ מִצְוָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the scope of רבי יאשיה's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even laxness in a single מצוה leads to weakness on a day of trouble.
steps.whatToRemember: The punishment of lacking strength in hard times applies not only to neglecting Torah study, but even to slacking off in one מצוה.

steps.title: חנינא sets the calendar outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו tells a story. When חנינא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, went down to בבל, he declared leap years and set new months there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: רבי אבהו used to tell: When חנינא, the son of רבי יהושע's brother, went down to the exile, he would declare leap years and set months outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The גמרא is setting up the background: חנינא was doing in בבל something that is normally done only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Declaring leap years and setting the months normally belongs to the בית דין of ארץ ישראל. By doing this in בבל, חנינא was creating a rival center of authority. The rest of the story shows how the חכמים of ארץ ישראל responded.

keyTerms.meaning: Declaring leap years, adding a month to the year
Fixing the start of new months

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume this story is praising חנינא. Setting the calendar outside ארץ ישראל was a serious problem. That is why the חכמים send people after him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה מִשְׁתַּעֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Safra said: Rabbi Abbahu would relate:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁיָּרַד חֲנִינָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לַגּוֹלָה,
phrases.english: When Ḥanina, son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother, went down to the Diaspora,
he would intercalate years and establish months
outside of Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה מִשְׁתַּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new narrative unrelated to the previous teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Background of the story: חנינא was fixing the calendar in בבל.

steps.title: Two scholars are sent after חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל send two scholars to חנינא. When he asks why they came, they say they came to learn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent after him two Torah scholars, רבי יוסי בן כיפר and the grandson of זכריה בן קבוטל. When he saw them, he said to them: Why did you come? They said to him: We came to learn Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. Messengers arrive, and at first they hide their real mission by saying they came to learn from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messengers do not openly confront חנינא at first. Their humble answer makes him trust them, and that sets up his public praise of them in the next step.

phrases.english: They sent after him two Torah scholars,
Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן בְּנוֹ שֶׁל זְכַרְיָה בֶּן קְבוּטָל.
phrases.english: and the grandson of Zekharya ben Kevutal.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה אוֹתָם, אָמַר לָהֶם: לָמָּה בָּאתֶם?
phrases.english: When he saw them, he said to them: Why did you come?
They said to him: We came to study Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the narrative with the response of the חכמים of ארץ ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The messengers present themselves as students who came to learn.

steps.title: חנינא publicly praises the visitors
steps.stepSummary: Flattered by their answer, חנינא announces that these men are great scholars of the generation and that their fathers served in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He announced about them: These men are the great ones of the generation, and their fathers served in the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: חנינא builds up the visitors' honor in front of everyone. This prepares for the next part of the story, where his praise will matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the scholars said they came to learn from him, חנינא felt honored and praised them publicly. Now the people of בבל respect these men, which will give weight to whatever they say later.

keyTerms.meaning: The great scholars of the generation

phrases.english: He proclaimed about them:
These men are the great ones of the generation,
and their fathers served in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: חנינא's reaction to the messengers' answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנינא publicly establishes the visitors' prestige.

steps.title: Proof that זכריה בן קבוטל served in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The text supports the claim about the visitors' ancestors by quoting a משנה in which זכריה בן קבוטל says he often read before the כהן גדול from ספר דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: זכריה בן קבוטל says: Many times I read before him from ספר דניאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A source is quoted to show that the grandfather of one of the visitors really did serve in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote comes from מסכת יומא. On the night of יום כיפור, זכריה בן קבוטל read to the כהן גדול to keep him awake. This confirms that the visitor's family had a place of honor in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (introducing a תנאי source)
I read before him (the כהן גדול)

phrases.english: As we learned:
Zekharya ben Kevutal says:

phrases.aramaic: הַרְבֵּה פְּעָמִים קָרִיתִי לְפָנָיו, בְּסֵפֶר דָּנִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Many times I read before him from the book of Daniel.
phrases.notes: "Him" means the כהן גדול on the night of יום כיפור (יומא פרק א).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports חנינא's claim that the visitors' fathers served in the מקדש
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the visitors' ancestors served in the בית המקדש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in יומא quoting זכריה בן קבוטל, who read before the כהן גדול

steps.title: The visitors rule against every ruling חנינא makes
steps.stepSummary: The two scholars begin ruling the opposite of חנינא. When he rules impure, they rule pure. When he forbids, they permit.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would rule something impure, and they would rule it pure. He would forbid something, and they would permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The two visitors he just praised now openly oppose every ruling חנינא gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the visitors looked like humble students. Now they reveal why they came: to weaken his authority by contradicting him in public. This sets up the conflict that drives the rest of the story.

phrases.english: He began ruling impure, and they ruling pure;
phrases.notes: Meaning: whatever he ruled, they ruled the opposite.

phrases.english: he forbidding, and they permitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after חנינא publicly praised the visitors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The visitors systematically contradict חנינא's rulings.

steps.title: חנינא publicly denounces the visitors
steps.stepSummary: חנינא announces that these men are worthless and know nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He announced about them: These men are worthless; they are good for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: Angry at being contradicted, חנינא reverses his earlier praise and declares the visitors worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 39 he called them great men of the generation. Now he tries to take that back. This reversal is what the visitors answer in the next step.

phrases.english: He announced about them:
These men are worthless;
they are good for nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the visitors' opposition and reverses the praise from Step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנינא tries to discredit the visitors in public.

steps.title: The visitors say he cannot take back his praise
steps.stepSummary: The visitors answer that he has already built up their reputation, so he cannot now tear it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You already built, and you cannot tear down. You already put up a fence, and you cannot break through it.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors reject חנינא's attempt to discredit them. His own public praise has already set up their reputation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They use images of building and fencing. Once he declared them great scholars, that statement stands, and his new insult cannot cancel it. His earlier flattery now works against him.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר בָּנִיתָ וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לִסְתּוֹר,
phrases.english: You have already built, and you cannot tear down;
phrases.notes: You already built up our reputation.

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר גָּדַרְתָּ וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לִפְרוֹץ.
phrases.english: you have already fenced, and you cannot break through.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר בָּנִיתָ וְאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לִסְתּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects חנינא's denunciation from Step 42.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects חנינא's attempt to take back his public praise.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He already established their status in public, so his new insult cannot undo it.

steps.title: חנינא asks why they always rule against him
steps.stepSummary: חנינא asks the visitors directly why they contradict every ruling he gives.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Why is it that I rule impure and you rule pure, I forbid and you permit?
steps.whatsHappening: Unable to discredit them, חנינא asks for the reason behind their opposition. This question sets up their main complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their opposition is clearly deliberate, not an honest difference of opinion. His question brings out their real motive.

phrases.english: He said to them: Why is it that
I rule impure and you rule pure,
I forbid and you permit?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֲנִי מְטַמֵּא וְאַתֶּם מְטַהֲרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from insults to asking the reason for the visitors' behavior.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the visitors oppose all of his rulings.

steps.title: Their reason: he sets the calendar outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The visitors explain that they oppose him because he sets leap years and new months in חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Because you make leap years and set the months outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors reveal their real complaint: setting the Jewish calendar belongs in ארץ ישראל, and חנינא is doing it in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to Step 37. Their constant contradiction was a protest, meant to show that he has stepped beyond his authority. If he can usurp the calendar, they can challenge his rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: declares leap years by adding a month
fixes the start of new months

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the principle behind the whole story: the calendar must be set by the authority of ארץ ישראל, so that the Jewish people stay unified.

phrases.english: They said to him: Because you
make leap years and set the months
outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאַתָּה מְעַבֵּר שָׁנִים וְקוֹבֵעַ חֳדָשִׁים בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חנינא's question from Step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They oppose him because he sets the calendar outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: חנינא points to רבי עקיבא as a precedent
steps.stepSummary: חנינא objects that רבי עקיבא also set leap years and months outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: But didn't עקיבא בן יוסף make leap years and set months outside the Land?
steps.whatsHappening: חנינא challenges their complaint with a precedent. A great sage did exactly what he is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If setting the calendar outside ארץ ישראל is forbidden, how could רבי עקיבא have done it? The challenge suggests the act is sometimes allowed, so חנינא should be allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי עקיבא, called by his full name

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: וַהֲלֹא עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: He said to them: But didn't Akiva ben Yosef
make leap years and set months
outside the Land!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף הָיָה מְעַבֵּר שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 45.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that setting the calendar outside ארץ ישראל is improper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Precedent: רבי עקיבא did the same thing, so it must be permitted.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא was different: he left no equal behind
steps.stepSummary: The visitors answer that רבי עקיבא was an exception, because no one his equal remained in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Leave רבי עקיבא aside, because he did not leave anyone like him in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors answer the challenge by setting רבי עקיבא's case apart from חנינא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the calendar outside the Land is allowed only when the greatest sage is there and no one of his level remains in ארץ ישראל. רבי עקיבא met that condition, so his case does not prove anything general.

phrases.english: They said to him: Leave Rabbi Akiva aside,
for he did not leave anyone like him in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנַּח רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחַ כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 46.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the precedent (אוקימתא of the exceptional case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's practice shows that anyone may set the calendar outside the Land.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is allowed only when no equal sage remains in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: חנינא claims he too left no equal behind
steps.stepSummary: חנינא answers that he, like רבי עקיבא, left no one his equal in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I also did not leave anyone like me in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: חנינא accepts their condition but says he meets it, so he should be allowed the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is no longer about the rule itself. Both sides now agree on the condition. The only question is a fact: is חנינא really greater than everyone left in ארץ ישראל?

phrases.english: He said to them: I too
did not leave anyone like me in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא הִנַּחְתִּי כְּמוֹתִי בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the condition from Step 47 to claim the same exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between רבי עקיבא and חנינא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנינא says he fits the same condition, so the distinction fails.

steps.title: His former students have grown greater than he is
steps.stepSummary: The visitors answer that the young students he left behind have grown into great scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: The young goats you left behind have become horned goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors deny the fact חנינא claimed. There are now scholars in ארץ ישראל of his level and higher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The image is of young goats who grew into strong, horned goats. When חנינא left, they were students, but they have since grown into leading sages. So the רבי עקיבא exception no longer applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: with horns, meaning strong and powerful

phrases.english: They said to him: The young goats you left behind
have become goats with horns,

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדָיִים שֶׁהִנַּחְתָּ נַעֲשׂוּ תְּיָשִׁים בַּעֲלֵי קַרְנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers חנינא's claim from Step 48 by denying the fact.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual rebuttal: the condition no longer holds
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חנינא is still the greatest sage, so he may set the calendar abroad.
steps.terutzMaskana: His students have grown greater, so he no longer has that authority.

steps.title: The ultimatum: obey, or be placed in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: The visitors say the sages of ארץ ישראל sent them with a message: if חנינא obeys, good; if not, he will be put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they sent us to you, and this is what they told us: Go and tell him in our name: If he listens, good; and if not, he will be in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The visitors finish the argument with an official message from the חכמים of ארץ ישראל: stop setting the calendar, or face נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here the exchange was a debate. Now the visitors show that they speak with official authority. The great sages חנינא left behind demand that he submit to the authority of ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: The calendar must be set by the authority of ארץ ישראל. A sage outside the Land may do it only when no one of his level remains there, as in רבי עקיבא's case. Once greater sages arose in ארץ ישראל, חנינא lost that right and was threatened with נידוי.

phrases.english: and they sent us to you,
and this is what they told us:
Go and tell him in our name:
If he listens, good;
and if not, he will be in excommunication.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 49: the great sages mentioned there are the ones who sent this ultimatum.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל require חנינא to stop setting the calendar in בבל, or else he will be placed in נידוי.
